chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Hafs al-Awsy al-Kufi, he raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah will not Honour (anyone) by ignorance at all, nor would He Humiliate (anyone) by forbearance at all'.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between ignorance, honor, and forbearance in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi’s chapter on Forbearance, this Prophetic saying establishes a divine principle where honor (izzah) is intrinsically linked to wisdom rather than mere status, while humiliation (dhull) is the natural consequence of lacking patience. Shia scholars often contrast this with the worldly notion that power brings honor, emphasizing that true elevation comes from intellectual and spiritual depth, whereas enduring hardship without forbearance leads to degradation. This hadith serves as a cornerstone for understanding the ethical framework of character development in Twelver Shi'ism.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ali Bin Hafs Al Awsy Al Kufy, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will not Honour (anyone) by ignorance at all, nor would He<sup>azwj</sup> Humiliate (anyone) by forbearance at all’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn Hafs al-‘Awsi al-Kufi in a marfu’ manner from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘
Allah has never given respect to anyone because of ignorance and He has never humiliated anyone who possessed forbearance.’”
